children: Visa
is reportedly in advanced talks to acquire crypto infrastructure company Fireblocks for about
$2.5 billion
, in a deal that could deepen the payments giant's push into stablecoins and digital-asset infrastructure.
Axios Pro reported Thursday that Visa is discussing a potential acquisition of Fireblocks, citing multiple sources.
Fireblocks provides technology that helps companies
hold, tokenize and transfer digital assets
and says it has processed roughly
$16 trillion in transactions across 2,500 customers
The reported price would represent a steep discount to Fireblocks' last private valuation.
The company was valued at about
$8 billion in 2022
following a fundraising round led by D1 Capital Partners and Spark Capital.
However, Fireblocks pushed back on the report.
This is news to us, and not true at present time, a spokesperson told CoinDesk, according to reports.
That denial makes the situation important to treat as
reported deal talks rather than a confirmed transaction
The potential combination would nevertheless fit Visa's broader digital-asset strategy.
In July, the company introduced an enterprise platform designed to give financial institutions, fintechs and crypto companies access to stablecoin capabilities through a Visa-managed environment.
Investor Takeaway
I think the strategic logic here is more interesting than the reported purchase price.
Visa already sits at the center of global payments.
Owning infrastructure that handles stablecoin custody, tokenization and transfers could give it deeper control over another layer of the emerging digital-payments stack.
The reported valuation is also notable.
Buying Fireblocks for around $2.5 billion would be far below its
$8 billion private-market valuation from 2022
, potentially giving Visa an opportunity to acquire mature crypto infrastructure at a reset valuation.
But investors should be careful not to get ahead of the facts.
Fireblocks has denied that the report is true at present, and there is no announced agreement.
For Visa investors, the key things to watch are
whether discussions are formally confirmed, the eventual deal price, regulatory scrutiny and how directly Fireblocks could accelerate Visa's stablecoin strategy
If a deal does emerge, it would be another sign that stablecoins are moving closer to the core of traditional payments.

title: Visa Makes Bold $2.5 Billion Bet on Future of Money
